pair_families.name: scissors_curve
pair_families.description: Straight versus curved scissor-like tools under tray-like overhead rendering.

pair_families.name: clamp_curve
pair_families.description: Straight versus curved clamp or hemostat-like tools with similar handles and shafts.

pair_families.name: tip_width
pair_families.description: Narrow-tip versus broad-tip tweezer or plier-like tools with subtle jaw differences.

stages.name: synthetic_seen_condition
stages.description: Train and test inside the same synthetic domain while holding out rendered scene instances only.
stages.rationale: This is the floor stage. It asks whether the detector can separate the target similar classes at all inside one simulator setup.
stages.what_it_proves: Success here means interpolation within the simulator, not robustness beyond it.
stages.mesh_policy: Meshes may overlap between train and test unless separate mesh variants are explicitly annotated.
stages.instance_policy: Synthetic scene instances are held out between train, val, and test.
stages.condition_policy: Lighting, roughness, and tray conditions are drawn from the same seen synthetic condition pool.

stages.name: synthetic_heldout_condition
stages.description: Train on one synthetic condition subset and test on held-out lighting, material, or background settings.
stages.rationale: This stage isolates synthetic robustness by withholding rendering conditions rather than only scene instances.
stages.what_it_proves: Success here means the model learned more than one rendering setup and can generalize to held-out synthetic conditions.
stages.mesh_policy: Use shared or held-out mesh variants according to the source manifest; record mesh_split in samples.csv for auditability.
stages.instance_policy: Synthetic scene instances remain held out between train, val, and test.
stages.condition_policy: Test examples come from held-out lighting, material, background, or camera-condition buckets.

stages.name: synthetic_to_real_transfer_pretrain
stages.description: Synthetic pretraining source used before fine-tuning on the matched small real dataset.
stages.rationale: This stage provides the synthetic initialization for the transfer comparison and should stay visually simple and tray-like in v1.
stages.what_it_proves: By itself this stage does not prove transfer. It is only the pretraining source for the matched fine-tuning comparison.
stages.mesh_policy: Prefer multiple mesh variants per class. Record held-out mesh variants when available.
stages.instance_policy: Synthetic scene instances are held out between train, val, and test splits.
stages.condition_policy: Domain randomization should vary lighting, roughness, camera distance, rotation, and tray texture without aiming for full OR realism.

stages.name: synthetic_to_real_transfer_real_small
stages.description: Small real proxy dataset used for both real-only training and synthetic-pretrain-plus-real fine-tuning, with unknown distractors reserved for evaluation.
stages.rationale: This stage holds the small real dataset constant so the only intended difference is whether synthetic pretraining happened first.
stages.what_it_proves: Improvement of synthetic_pretrain_plus_real_small over real_small_from_scratch is the main evidence that simulation is useful when real data is scarce.
stages.mesh_policy: Meshes do not apply directly; record proxy-family or asset identifiers if available.
stages.instance_policy: Prefer holding out physical instances. If unavailable, hold out sessions and conditions and document the limitation.
stages.condition_policy: Keep the real proxy set tray-like, modest in size, and paired with unknown similar distractor images in the test split.
